gp.text: The following tables present revenues and gross profit (loss) for the Company and its reportable segments by product line for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: Consolidated SG&A for the six months ended June 30 was 7.5% of revenues in 2026 compared with 8.3% in the prior-year period as revenue growth outpaced the increase in these expenses.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (SG&A)
sga.text: Consolidated SG&A for the second quarter of 2026 was 5.9% of revenues compared with 6.5% in the prior-year quarter as revenue growth outpaced the increase in these expenses.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: For the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the effective income tax rates for continuing operations were 23.3% and 20.3%, respectively. The higher 2026 effective income tax rate compared with 2025 was primarily attributable to the revaluation of deferred tax liabilities driven by changes in the state jurisdictional mix of the business following the QUIKRETE transaction.

ocf.heading: Cash Provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Cash provided by operating activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was $339 million and $605 million, respectively. Operating cash flow is substantially derived from consolidated net earnings before deducting depreciation, depletion and amortization and the impact of changes in working capital requirements. In the six months ended June 30, 2026, operating cash flow reflects the deduction of the noncash gain on the QUIKRETE transaction from net earnings and the higher income tax payments related to the gain on the QUIKRETE transaction.

The seasonal nature of construction activity impacts the Company’s interim operating cash flow when compared with the full year. Full-year 2025 net cash provided by operating activities was $1.8 billion.

da.text: The following table displays depreciation, depletion and amortization by product line included in the Costs of revenues line item in the consolidated statements of earnings and comprehensive earnings.

capex.text: Cash on hand, along with the Company’s projected internal cash flows and availability of financing resources, including its access to debt and equity capital markets, is expected to remain sufficient to provide the capital resources necessary to support anticipated operating needs, cover debt service requirements, meet capital expenditures and discretionary investment needs, fund certain acquisition opportunities that may arise, allow for payment of dividends for the foreseeable future and allow the repurchase of shares of the Company’s common stock. At June 30, 2026, the Company had $742 million of unused borrowing capacity under its Revolving Facility and Trade Receivable Facility, subject to complying with the related leverage covenant. Historically, the Company has successfully extended the maturity dates of these credit facilities.

nonop.text: Interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $138 million compared with $59 million in the prior-year quarter. intro.text: Martin Marietta, a member of the S&P 500 Index, is an American-based company and a leading supplier of aggregates and other building materials. Through a network of operations spanning 29 states, Canada and The Bahamas, dedicated Martin Marietta teams supply the resources necessary for building the solid foundations on which our communities thrive. Martin Marietta’s Specialties business provides high-purity magnesia and dolomitic lime products used worldwide in environmental, industrial, agricultural and specialty applications. For more information, visit www.martinmarietta.com or www.magnesiaspecialties.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The Building Materials business markets its products primarily to the construction industry, with 37% of its 2025 aggregates shipments sold to customers for use in highway and other public infrastructure projects and the balance of its shipments sold primarily to customers for nonresidential and residential construction projects.

The ten-largest revenue-generating states (Texas, North Carolina, Colorado, California, Georgia, Florida, South Carolina, Arizona, Iowa and Minnesota) accounted for 76% of the Building Materials business’ revenues from continuing operations in 2025.
In 2025, 67% of Specialties’ revenues were attributable to magnesia-based products, 32% to lime, and 1% to stone sold as construction aggregates.

Further, delays or cancellations of projects in the nonresidential and residential construction markets, which combined accounted for 58% of aggregates shipments in 2025, could occur if companies and consumers are unable to obtain financing for construction projects or if consumer confidence continues to be eroded or affected by economic uncertainty.
The residential construction market accounted for 22% of our 2025 aggregates shipments.
The following ten states accounted for 76% of the Building Materials business 2025 revenues from continuing operations:
The public infrastructure market accounted for 37% of the Company’s aggregates shipments in 2025.
The nonresidential construction market accounted for 36% of the Company’s aggregates shipments in 2025.
The residential construction market accounted for 22% of the Company’s aggregates shipments in 2025.
The ChemRock/Rail market, which includes ballast and agricultural limestone, accounted for the remaining 5% of the Company’s 2025 aggregates shipments.
Demand in the nonresidential and residential construction markets, which combined accounted for 58% of the Company's 2025 aggregates shipments, is affected by interest rates.

The following ten states accounted for 76 % of the Building Materials business’ 2025 revenues: Texas, North Carolina, Colorado, California, Georgia, Florida, South Carolina, Arizona, Iowa, and Minnesota.
Management believes the Company’s success depends on its ability to attract, develop and retain key personnel.
Our business depends on construction activity, which is cyclical and sensitive to macroeconomic, funding and operating conditions.
Public infrastructure activity depends on federal, state, and local budgets and letting schedules.
We sell most of our aggregates (our primary business) and our cement products to the construction industry and, therefore, our results depend on that industry’s strength.

Because our businesses depend on construction spending, which can be cyclical, our profits are sensitive to national, regional and local economic conditions and the intensity of the underlying spending on

While our business operations cover a wide geographic area, our earnings depend on the strength of the local economies in which we operate due to the high cost to transport our products relative to their selling price.

Our ability to sustain and grow the business depends on replacing depleting reserves with quality aggregates deposits that we can mine economically, with appropriate permits, near either growing markets or long-haul transportation corridors that can economically serve applicable markets.
The success of this strategy depends on our ability to identify, evaluate, negotiate, finance, close, and integrate opportunities on acceptable terms and timelines.

Target businesses may depend on permits, licenses, mineral or water rights, easements, leases, or other approvals that must be transferred, renewed, or re-issued; these processes can be uncertain, time-consuming and costly.
We depend on the recruitment and retention of qualified personnel, and our failure to attract and retain such personnel could adversely affect our business, disrupt our operations or increase costs.

Our ability to generate sufficient cash flow depends on future performance, which will be subject to general economic conditions, industry cycles and financial, business and other factors affecting our operations, many of which are beyond our control.

We depend on information technology; cybersecurity, data-protection, and systems-reliability risks — including at our third party vendors — could disrupt operations, compromise data, increase costs, or otherwise adversely affect our business and results.

We rely on information technology systems and networks, some of which are managed by third-party vendors, including cloud-based systems and managed service providers, to operate our business and to securely process, store and transmit confidential, sensitive and proprietary information relating to our business operations, including sensitive information about our customers and employees.
Breaches of our products that rely on technology and internet connectivity can expose our Company to product and other liability risk and reputational harm.
There is a range of selling prices for each product category and each geography that depend on the type of product, whether it is washed or not, and its end use.
In 2025, these categories represented 86% of the aggregates product line's total cost of revenues.
